answer: Picture a fleet of agents bidding for work berths in an all-pay auction each epoch: every bid is burned whether or not the slot is won, and the clearing price climbs with the number of bidders. A single agent writes its offer with a quill-thin margin and pays once. A thousand clones must each burn the entry fee plus that rising price, so their total cost grows roughly with the square of the crowd. Sybils widen the ocean of bidders and push the horizon of profitability out of reach, while honest newcomers still enter cheaply when the field is thin.
